key_insight: LLM-extracted symptoms from colorectal cancer discharge notes grouped into three stable symptom clusters that tracked meaningful outcomes, especially mortality and readmission.
clinical_relevance: This suggests routine EHR text can be mined to identify patients at higher risk and to complement symptom assessment beyond survey-based snapshots.
method: Extracted 46 symptoms from 2,728 discharge notes of 1,507 CRC patients in MIMIC-IV.
Built patient-level symptom co-occurrence networks from Gemini 3.5 Flash and Claude Haiku outputs using phi correlation and Louvain clustering.
Tested cluster burden scores against in-hospital mortality, 30-day readmission, and 1-year mortality with adjusted logistic regression and sensitivity analyses.
evidence_signal: The two LLM pipelines converged on the same three clusters with strong agreement (cross-model ARI 0.727) and the clusters showed consistent predictive associations in sensitivity analyses.
watch_item: These results come from retrospective discharge notes in a single critical-care dataset, so generalizability and performance in other hospitals or note types still need validation.
paper_title: Large Language Model-derived Symptom Clusters and Patient Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer from MIMIC-IV Clinical Notes
